name: Boeing 767-300ER

reference.engine: GE CF6-80C2 (ACAP engine-inlet dimension used: GE 18.54 m)
reference.notes: Reference = Boeing factory configuration shown in ACAP D6-58328 (Rev I used) section 2.2.2: plain wingtip, no winglet. Aviation Partners blended winglet retrofit exists (certified 2009; a trade report of roughly 217 767-300ER fitted, undated, circa 2012-13), but I could not verify fleet shares today, so 'none' is chosen as the documented configuration; this is an inference, not a counted fact. If drawing a winglet variant, treat it as an overlay, not geometry in this record. Engine choice CF6-80C2 vs PW4000 is also unverified by fleet counts; the ACAP gives inlet x for both (RR/PW 18.72 m, GE 18.54 m) and nacelle outline is near-identical at drawing scale. Distinctive 767 traits: small round nacelle (about 2.8 m, pod sits close under the wing, gap to wing about 0.5 m), narrow 5.03 m fuselage with a 5.41 m height (taller than wide by 0.4 m, slightly oval front view), a long rounded nose with cockpit side windows ending near x=3 m, wing LE sweep about 35 deg with a trailing-edge kink at y about 7.5 m, tail with a smooth dorsal-style fillet but no distinct dorsal fin, tip rounded and plain. Overall length 54.94 m includes the horizontal-stab tip; the fuselage itself ends near x=53.7 m (measured). Tail height: ACAP gives a range 15.39-16.03 m depending on attitude; Boeing's 767 page lists 15.85 m (listed on the 767F page, same airframe family), used here.

reference.notes: Reference = ACAP D6-58333 Rev Q (Oct 2025) section 2.2.1 787-8 drawing, raked wingtip, nacelles with chevrons on the fan and core nozzles. GEnx-1B chosen because a web article (eplaneai, undated) says about 34 percent of 787s in service use Rolls-Royce, implying roughly two thirds GE; this is a single secondary source, not a fleet count. The ACAP general-dimension drawing does not distinguish the two engines (ground clearance F differs slightly: GE 0.74-1.07 m, RR 0.71-1.07 m). Distinctive 787 traits: smooth, more rounded nose with a four-pane cockpit glazing (two large forward panes and two side panes; the glazing shows as a shallow slanted band, side windows end near x=3.1 m), no pronounced nose 'chin' break, a long gently curving trailing edge with no sharp Yehudi kink (kinkY is the point where TE starts to sweep aft, about y=9.5 m), highly swept raked tip that ends in a pointed trailing corner (tip LE x 37.69 m, TE x 40.36 m per ACAP), large round nacelle (about 3.95 m) with sawtooth chevrons on the fan and core nozzle trailing edges, and a high-aspect, strongly upswept tail cone ending in a rounded (not blade) point. Overall length 56.72 m is to the horizontal-stab tip; the fuselage ends near x=55.91 m (ACAP side-view dimension). Tail height 16.92 m is the nominal ACAP figure; the clearance table gives 16.59-17.09 m. Raked-tip LE departs the straight LE near y=27.7 m (rakeSpan measured as tip y 30.06 minus 27.7). v3: noseExponent measured from the plan silhouette (plan view only). v4: tip rebuilt from wingtip.rakeLE / rakeTE measured on ACAP p.2-5. The two ACAP markers (LE 37.69, TE 40.36) are not a 2.67 m tip chord: the LE passes x = 37.69 at y = 28.9, 1.16 m inboard of the pointed tip corner (40.36, 30.06). Straight LE refit to the same plan raster (rootLEx 18.8, sweep 34.9). Stabiliser: rootY 1.8, sweep fitted to the measured tip LE 55.17 / TE 56.72.

name: Boeing 777-300ER

reference.notes: Reference = ACAP D6-58329-2 Rev G (Dec 2024) section 2.2.2 777-300ER drawing; GE90-115B is the only engine offered on the -300ER. Nacelle diameter: the ACAP drawing gives no diameter label (the '13 ft 0 in (3.96 m)' dimension in the front view is the gap between main gear and nacelle, not a diameter). Measured off the ACAP front and side views the outer nacelle is about 3.8 m (front view 3.73 m outer circle, side view 3.86 m). Wikipedia lists GE90 'maximum width' 3.769 m (consistent) but also states a nacelle maximum diameter of 166 in (4.2 m) for the higher-thrust variants; that 4.2 m is unverified for the -115B and conflicts with the ACAP drawing, so 3.8 m is used. Fan diameter is 128 in (3.25-3.3 m), not used. Distinctive 777 traits: very large round nacelle (about 3.8 m) sitting close beneath the wing; the long fuselage constant section with a slender nose; a tail cone that ends in a flat, blade-shaped (vertical-knife) cone, upswept by about 2.3 m and extending rearward of the fuselage end at x=73.08 m, hence the overall length 73.86 m reaching the horizontal-stab tip; a smooth wing with a long straight leading edge (sweep about 34 deg), a pronounced kink in the trailing edge near y=11 m, and a pointed raked tip: LE rake begins near y=31.1 m, TE rake near y=29.9 m, tip LE x 48.50 m, tip TE x 49.11 m (ACAP) so tip chord is 0.61 m at the very point. Tail height: ACAP ground-clearance table gives 18.24-18.85 m (attitude range, no nominal); the maximum 18.85 m is stored; nominal not verified. Wheelbase/landing gear (six-wheel main bogies) not drawn. v3: noseExponent measured from the plan silhouette (plan view only; applied to the side profile too). v4: wingtip.rakeLE / rakeTE added (LE rake start (46.20, 31.30), tip LE (48.50, 32.40); TE rake break (47.36, 29.86), tip TE (49.11, 32.40)) measured on the ACAP p.2-4 vector plan; straight LE sweep 34.4. Stabiliser: rootY 1.9, rootLEx 64.25, rootChord 6.3, sweep fitted to tip LE 71.58 / TE 73.86 (overall length is to the stabiliser tip).
